children: , Hewlett Packard Enterprise (NYSE:HPE) and HP Inc.

jumped 8% or more Friday as investors bet that enterprise AI spending, server upgrades and a broad PC refresh are creating a multi-year demand cycle for hardware vendors. The rally reflects growing evidence that AI infrastructure spending is expanding beyond hyperscalers into traditional enterprise computing.
Dell received a fresh Outperform rating and a $640 price target from RBC Capital Markets, which pointed to the company's massive AI server backlog and continued supply constraints.

"DELL exited 2Q27 with $95bn in AI server backlog and a pipeline that continues to grow despite converting ~$132bn into orders over the LTM," RBC analyst David Paige said. "We view the environment as supply-constrained (primarily memory) rather than demand-limited and expect a meaningful backlog to persist through FY27, providing visibility into FY28."
RBC also sees agentic AI supporting demand for traditional servers, not just GPU-heavy systems.
"Agentic AI is creating incremental CPU/traditional server demand to run orchestration layers, expanding the TAM for traditional compute," Paige added.
HPE gained additional support from Oracle's

strong results. Oracle recently agreed to deploy HPE routing and switching equipment across its data centers as it scales AI infrastructure. Oracle's remaining performance obligations climbed to $664 billion after adding more than $30 billion of AI cloud contracts, potentially creating a substantial networking opportunity for HPE.

HP, meanwhile, received a Sector Perform rating and $33 target from RBC. The bank expects AI PCs, edge computing and data-privacy requirements to support demand, with HP targeting AI PCs at 60% to 70% of shipments by fiscal 2027, up from roughly 45% in the latest quarter.
For Dell, the key metrics are AI server backlog conversion, memory availability and whether traditional server demand accelerates alongside AI systems.
HPE investors should monitor Oracle-related networking deployments and broader AI data-center orders, while HP's case depends on enterprise PC replacement rates and AI-PC adoption.

The larger risk is that current enthusiasm assumes a durable multi-year refresh cycle. Any slowdown in enterprise AI spending, component shortages or weaker PC demand could quickly challenge that thesis.

title: RBC Drops Jaw Dropping Price Target on Dell Stock
